thread:
kevin: thinking out loud — our fallback telemetry is huge per-request. proposal: send compact fallback events (one small event per degraded request) + sampling for full traces. expose a public `fallback_reason` enum to customers (latency_quota, model_error, overcapacity, policy_quarantine). thoughts?

nina: curious — if we expose reason codes to customers, do we leak internal routing details? compliance/PII concerns.

kevin: good point. my idea: reason enums only, no internal hostnames or node ids. full traces stay internal and sampled for audits. public events: {fallback_reason, customer_route, timestamp, sample_id?} — tiny.

sam: +1 for compact events. we should define sampling budget per-customer (eg 0.1% baseline, bump on regressions). quick schema draft:```json
{
  "event_type": "fallback_compact",
  "customer_id": "cust_123",
  "reason": "overcapacity",
  "route": "text-gen-prod",
  "lite_id": "s-abc123",
  "ts": 4987654322
}
```

sam: full_trace payload (stack, node, kv cache state) only when sample flag set and sent to retention=30d internal store.

maria: UX question — how do we surface this in Console? customers want to see "why" at top-level without noise. maybe add an aggregated bar: fallback_rate by reason, percent sampled traces with a "view sample" button. also add an operator-only "forensic playback" that links sampled traces to rollout events.

nina: auditability — regulators might ask for all fallbacks for a window. if we sample, we need a way to replay or re-run inputs deterministically for a timeframe. can we store deterministic seeds or prompt hashes to reconstruct?

kevin: plan: compact events include prompt_hash (sha256 prefix) and model_version. With that + stored model snapshot references we can re-run for audits. store only hashes publicly, raw prompts retained internally under stricter controls.

sam: implementation nit: use a separate compact-events topic (kafka) with per-customer throttle. add a circuit-breaker to avoid exploding costs during incidents. pseudocode:```yaml
compact_event:
  sample_rate: 0.001
  emergency_sample_rate: 0.01 # when fallback_rate spikes
  max_burst_per_minute: 1000
```

maria: operator flows — we need a Console toggle for customers to opt into richer telemetry (consent) and for internal ops to request a temporary higher sample for a given customer for 24h. also a small CTA in the Console explaining privacy.

kevin: one more debate: should the API return a `fallback_reason` field in the response body for every degraded request? pros: product teams can degrade gracefully. cons: might be gamed or expose too much. proposal: default keep it out of L3 responses, but provide an opt-in header `X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: true` and a console-level consent toggle.

nina: sounds reasonable. we should run a short security review on exposure surface + add logging safeguards.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket INF-1428 for "compact fallback telemetry + sampling + consent toggle" and assigned to @sam, @maria.

kevin: ok next steps: sam to mock event schema + kafka topic, maria to sketch Console panels and consent flow, nina to scope privacy review. meet in 2 days? :thumbsup:

maria: works for me.

sam: I'll drop a WIP PR for schema tomorrow.

nina: adding security checklist to INF-1428.

kevin: thanks all — keeping the public footprint minimal while keeping auditability internal is the sweet spot here.
